title: B.C. man shot by cops had hit list: Police
article: Police say a man who allegedly went on a murderous rampage in Burnaby, B.C., had a hit list with 10 other targets.

Angus David Mitchell, who police say killed three people and severely wounded another before being fatally shot by Mounties, had maps, addresses, and telephone numbers in his van with details of entry and escape routes on potential victims, said Insp. Kevin Hackett,
Every one of the 26-year-old's alleged targets had some conflict with him, dating back to 2009.

On May 27, Mitchell allegedly shot and killed a woman working at the Royal Oak Sushi House in Burnaby, along with the restaurant owner and a bystander. Mitchell's former landlord was shot and severely wounded two days later.
They were the first targets, Hackett said.
The "unusual and disturbing" case came to an abrupt halt on May 30, when tactical officers surrounded Mitchell in Maple Ridge, B.C., and killed him.
Susanne Murphy, whose 911 call tipped police to Mitchell's whereabouts, recalled her shock in coming within "five to 10 feet" of the gunman's Ford.

"I was really nervous ... I didn't know if he was in his van. I didn't know if he was walking around in the wooded area. I didn't know what to think," she said. "I just knew I had to call 911 and say, 'His van's here.'"
Hackett said there's no evidence any of Mitchell's former employers were on the list. He'd worked for a number of security companies.

Hackett also confirmed a rifle Mitchell brought to a Saanich, B.C., clinic, which was seized by Victoria police and returned several weeks later, was the same gun used in the Burnaby double homicide and attempted murder.
A homicide team media liaison, however, retracted that information shortly after.
"While we can say it appears to be the same type of firearm, investigators will not be able to confirm this information," she said.
The Vancouver Police Department continues its investigation into the clinic incident.
A spokesman also declined to disclose details on a warning related to a gun from one of Mitchell's former Vancouver roommates in September.
While the federal RCMP is responsible for gun permit licensing, local jurisdictions handle individual investigations in their municipalities, Mounties added.
